answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique notary commission record. With a commission with a journal of acts over years, a single beacon check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. What the farm fears is not one hard check but a check that cannot be shared: a commission with a journal of acts over years is per-account by construction, and the canyon is that the tenth clone costs as much as the first. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the hollow of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
